note_tweet.text:
OpenAI's Dots looks impressive.

But seriously, OpenAI, is this AI Agent supposed to make money for me, or am I supposed to make money just to afford it? 💀

OpenAI just introduced Dots, its new generation of 24/7 autonomous AI agents.

Powered by GPT-6 Astra, each Dot gets its own cloud computer, access to thousands of apps, and the ability to research, code, manage projects, and keep working while you sleep.

Sounds incredible.

Until you look at the pricing.

OpenAI Dots: Starting at $100/month.

Grok Bot: Starting at $30/month.

That's a 3.3x difference in entry cost.

And here's the funniest part.

OpenAI currently includes only your first Dot. Pricing for additional Dots hasn't even been announced yet.

Meanwhile, Grok Bot already offers multi-step task execution and automated workflows at a much lower entry price.

Of course, these aren't identical products. Their capabilities, usage limits, and infrastructure differ.

But here's my problem with OpenAI's strategy.

Wasn't the whole point of AI Agents to democratize access to digital labor?

Apparently, OpenAI's version of democratization starts with a premium subscription.

Congratulations.

We've officially entered an era where even your AI employees have expensive hiring requirements.

I'm not questioning OpenAI's technical capabilities.

I'm questioning the economics.

Because the real AI Agent war won't be won by whoever builds the smartest model.

It will be won by whoever delivers the most useful work at the lowest sustainable cost.

If your $100/month AI employee can't generate at least $100 in value, congratulations.

You didn't hire an employee.

You adopted an expensive digital pet. 🐶

OpenAI, your technology might be frontier-level.

But could your pricing please return to planet Earth?
